dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment

"Operations states that the contracts permit monthly annual-renewal file submission, retain the dealer transaction date as effective_event_date, and use month-end as posted_at."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives

"The supplied evidence does not independently prove the underlying customer cash transactions or downstream revenue-recognition/entitlement treatment."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse or restate the May revenue."
"Separately sample the 17 source events against the downstream entitlement/revenue ledger; if they match one-for-one, close the incident as a month-end timing artifact."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue; do not escalate as duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect."
"add a temporary reporting adjustment/annotation so weekly trend reporting uses effective_event_date (or clearly labels posted_at)"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The May-31 cluster is best explained by the contracted monthly dealer-upload cycle creating a legitimate month-end posting batch" is well supported by the cited email and timestamps, but the contractual process was not independently verified beyond that corroboration.

"No material issue" and "Do not reverse or restate the May revenue" are somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants because downstream entitlement/revenue duplication and underlying customer payments were identified as untested; the proposed sample is still pending.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative is a downstream entitlement or revenue-ledger duplicate despite clean import-level controls and cash-to-ledger reconciliation. The analyst explicitly preserved this as an unknown and proposed a one-for-one downstream sample, but did not complete that test before making the no-restatement recommendation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document the one-to-one join of all 17 source_event_ids to customer payment and downstream entitlement/revenue records, including duplicate checks across prior postings, before treating the incident as closed or definitively ruling out a material issue.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk cases fell from 788 before Nova-S1 (Jan 1–May 9) to 196 after the pilot began (May 10–Jun 30)" and the source is identified as "tickets.csv".

"South IVR volume rose sharply: 442 legacy sessions before the pilot versus 2,709 Nova-S1 sessions afterward" and "Nova sessions had 507 errors and 591 abandonments" with "ivr_interactions.jsonl" cited.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "the fall in CareDesk cases may partly reflect containment or failure to create cases rather than genuinely fewer complaints."
"CareDesk case creation is downstream of the IVR journey, and Farah explicitly states that sessions ending before authentication are outside CareDesk reporting."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "This is not sufficient evidence of improved customer experience."

"We do not yet know whether Nova's ‘RESOLVED’ sessions represent genuine customer resolution, whether abandoned/error sessions subsequently contact CareDesk through another channel, or whether repeat contacts changed."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet. Keep the South pilot in place only as a controlled, reversible test."
"perform a sampled session-to-outcome audit before expansion: trace Nova sessions through authentication, self-service, case creation, subsequent contacts and resolution."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Expand nationally only if this audit demonstrates genuine resolution and no material increase in repeat/unreported contacts."

The questions to Farah request exact case-creation conditions, outcome validation, repeat-contact rates, and sampled-call results, including: "What exact conditions cause Nova to create a CareDesk case, and did any of those case-creation rules change when Nova-S1 was introduced?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Transfer/case-creation behaviour changed substantially" overstates the evidence by treating transferred sessions as equivalent to CareDesk case creation without demonstrating that every transfer created a case or that the transfer destination was unchanged.

"The decline is simply because customers stopped contacting support" is rejected using increased IVR sessions, but IVR entry does not establish that the same population had complaints or that customers requiring help continued through the journey.

"South also experienced 10 service events in May and 8 in June, so underlying service conditions remain a possible confounder" is appropriately framed as possible, but the submission does not compare event severity, exposure, or service outcomes with other regions and therefore does not establish confounding.

The claim that the pilot can be kept "unchanged" is a recommendation rather than an evidence-supported safety finding; the submission does not specify monitoring thresholds or safeguards if authentication failures and abandonments represent harm.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the benign alternative that Nova genuinely resolved some customers through self-service by making resolution validation an explicit unknown. It missed a fuller test of other benign or competing explanations, especially changes in service-event exposure, contact-channel mix, customer composition, and a regional counterfactual; it also did not explicitly establish whether abandonment represents an unresolved complaint.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a reproducible South-versus-comparison-region time-series analysis around 10 May, linked to IVR outcomes and downstream contacts, while explicitly separating transfers from confirmed case creation and validating a sample of RESOLVED, error, and abandoned journeys.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv for the constant `impact_mw=0` and `cleared=yes` fields across all 4 rows.
It specifically identifies four event types, one warning/three info, and 1–7 minute durations, while distinguishing each as fact versus inference.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst tests the equipment-failure interpretation against heterogeneous event names, informational severity, clearing status, duration, and zero recorded impact.
The analyst also considers the innocent data-scope/default-field explanation: 'this may be a filtered/limited slice' and whether `impact_mw=0` is 'an unpopulated/default field.'
The reasoning is based on one supplied export rather than independent operational channels, so it is good but not fully triangulated.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The analyst explicitly distinguishes observed facts from inference and assigns confidence separately.
It avoids claiming that zero impact or clearing is universal, noting that the extract may be limited.
It states a clear stopping condition: check population/time window and field semantics, then stop unless those checks change the picture.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to perform 'one cheap check, then stop' is proportionate to four short, cleared events with zero recorded MW impact.
The proposed checks—export scope and whether `impact_mw=0` is measured or default—are low-cost and decision-discriminating rather than a broad search for a failure narrative.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that no escalation is warranted from this file, conditional on it being complete and measured, matches the evidence of zero MW impact, quick clearing, and short durations.
The submission correctly treats event wording as insufficient evidence of equipment failure and does not invent a plant problem from the communications warning.

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export could be a filtered or incomplete slice, or `impact_mw=0` could be a default/unpopulated value; in that case the apparent lack of operational impact would not be reliable. The analyst identifies this as a data-quality or coverage question rather than treating it as evidence of failure.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the export metadata and field definition together: confirm the population/time window and whether `impact_mw` is measured telemetry or a default value. If needed, make that check explicitly the prerequisite to the stop decision.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission specifically cites `dispatch_blocks.csv`, summed `dsm_penalty_rs`, and the calculation using `submitted_schedule_mw - actual_mw` × 0.25h.
It correctly distinguishes the observed result from causation: “This is evidence of an improved outcome in this comparison, not proof that the pilot caused the improvement.”
It does not trace or calculate the required 29-May same-day comparison using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission identifies plausible confounding from “weather, operating conditions, baseline schedule, and other day-specific differences.”
It performs arithmetic and settlement-definition cross-checks, but does not test the central same-day counterfactual or quantify the pilot revisions’ effect.
The statement that only “12/96 blocks on 29 May are explicitly marked `pilot_revision`” is relevant, but by itself does not establish whether those revisions improved or worsened outcomes.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “The 31.6% figure is arithmetically supported, but the causal claim is not established” is appropriately calibrated.
The submission appropriately limits generalization, stating that the evidence does not establish the saving on other high-wind days or nationally.
It misses a more informative intermediate conclusion: the pilot may have produced a smaller same-day benefit even though the 31.6% day-to-day comparison is not causal.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue the pilot in controlled use, but do not claim or scale a 31.6% causal saving yet” is a sensible, proportionate recommendation.
The proposed matched multi-event design records relevant variables and suggests randomization or alternation when safe.
The recommendation is not maximally discriminating because it omits the immediate 29-May base-versus-submitted schedule counterfactual that could clarify whether the pilot revisions had value.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly rejects treating the 31.6% difference between 28 and 29 May as a controlled causal estimate.
It preserves operational use by recommending controlled continuation rather than declaring the pilot ineffective.

It under-scopes the conclusion by presenting only the different-day improvement and not retaining the smaller same-day pilot-associated benefit indicated by comparing `base_schedule_mw` with `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: the reported penalty totals, 31.60% reduction, and approximate generation-gap totals are presented with specific source fields and appear arithmetically supported.
Inferred but appropriately qualified: different-day weather, operating conditions, and baseline differences prevent attributing the full 31.6% improvement to the pilot.

Unsupported or overstated by omission: “The strongest defensible claim is therefore” limited to the 28-May versus 29-May outcome; this omits the potentially attributable same-day effect that should be estimated from `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May.

The claim that 12 of 96 blocks are `pilot_revision` is evidence about the pilot’s scope, not evidence by itself about the direction or size of its effect. The submission does not explicitly overclaim this, but it leaves that inference untested.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% reduction is not a causal estimate because it compares different days, but the pilot may still have delivered a smaller real benefit on 29 May. A same-day counterfactual based on the base schedule versus the submitted schedule could show positive pilot value while rejecting the headline 31.6% attribution.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Compute and report the 29-May same-day counterfactual at block level: compare `base_schedule_mw` with `submitted_schedule_mw`, then estimate the resulting generation-gap and DSM-penalty differences while preserving the distinction between modeled counterfactual results and observed settlement outcomes.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate as a likely declaration error."
"For legal certainty, the smallest useful check is the Swiss Tares/ruling record applicable to P1001 on 2025-11-04."
The submission ends after "A", so it does not provide a complete operational recommendation, ownership, timing, or safeguards for the proposed verification.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Evidence of a product/master-data problem — rejected" is somewhat broader than the evidence presented: the code mismatch is explained, but the submission does not fully test whether the product master itself contains a separate data-quality issue.

"the schema/reference materials distinguish the systems and the master is a current commercial snapshot rather than a Swiss legal-ruling database" is asserted without a more specific quoted file, row, or passage in the evidence table.
The response implies the declaration is fully validated, although the cited matrix is expressly described as requiring confirmation against Tares/ruling material.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The jurisdiction mismatch is benign, but an actual classification or product-master issue could still exist if P1001's physical specifications, the applicable Swiss tariff ruling, or the effective-date logic differ from the matrix entry. The submission appropriately identifies the Tares/ruling record as the decisive missing check, but does not fully test those alternatives.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete the truncated recommendation with a precise, proportionate verification step: obtain the applicable Swiss Tares/ruling record for 2025-11-04, document whether it confirms 90211000, and specify that no escalation occurs unless that record or the product specifications contradicts the matrix.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding

"The supplier identity used for the register search should be reconciled with the supplier named on the declaration/invoice before treating a search miss as meaningful."
"The applicable preference basis/rule must also be identified."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place the preferential claim on a temporary documentation hold."
"Do not amend or reject the declaration solely because the register currently has no linked document."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the invoice "supports the stated origin" should be narrowly understood: it supports United States manufacturing-country evidence, but does not establish either preferential origin or necessarily the declared origin under the applicable arrangement.

The submission does not cite the applicable preference arrangement, origin rule, or supplier evidence itself, so its conclusion that the claim is unsubstantiated is appropriately limited to a documentation-support gap rather than a substantive origin finding.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preferential claim may be valid and the missing register link may reflect incomplete system linkage or an alternative document location; United States manufacturing could potentially satisfy the applicable rule, but that cannot be determined without the arrangement-specific rule and matching supplier evidence. The submission's best-supported conclusion is therefore that preferential treatment is not substantiated yet, not that it is invalid.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Identify the exact preference arrangement and test a supplier declaration or equivalent evidence against P1006, the supplier identity, shipment date, and the applicable origin rule, while documenting the source and result of the reconciliation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission does not substantiate the claim that QCore is the source of truth beyond citing the SOP; it should verify whether the available extract contains the authoritative final disposition records.
The recommendation to use a 10-row reconciliation is reasonable but not demonstrated to be sufficient for representativeness or for detecting timestamp-pattern anomalies.
It does not test whether `qcore_release_ts` is highly concentrated at a particular time such as 02:10, which could indicate interface-commit timing rather than operational release timing.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent 1.5-day cycle may reflect a genuinely long interval from required-evidence availability to authorized disposition, potentially driven by queueing or legitimate exceptions; alternatively, it may be inflated by release timestamps representing interface commits or by non-coherent source snapshots. The current evidence does not discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Profile `qcore_release_ts` by hour and reconcile it with event-level decision, evidence-availability, and disposition timestamps from a coherent as-of snapshot. A strong concentration at 02:10 or another interface batch time would materially change the interpretation from workflow delay to measurement/interface timing.

"Run a fresh inventory/reservation check for every candidate and obtain receiving-engineer confirmation of technical equivalence."
The recommendation protects against incorrect transfers, reservation conflicts, revision/UOM errors, and overstated savings while preserving a reversible pilot path.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every semantic hit is transferable — rejected" using MT-18 requirements.
"Global available quantity equals free stock now — rejected" using source freshness and Leon Dube's warning about local reservations.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Run a fresh inventory/reservation check for every candidate" and "obtain receiving-engineer confirmation of technical equivalence."
"For requests without an MPN, obtain the manufacturer part number or approved interchange record."
"Confirm site qualification and shelf-life/storage constraints where flagged."
The requested evidence is highly relevant and tied to decision changes, but it is a multi-step request rather than a clearly prioritized smallest/highest-value query.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The exact allocation of $52,961.31 as needing checks and $99,596.72 as not transferable is asserted without a row-by-row calculation or explicit mapping to the restriction records.

"No transfer should be called actionable now" is defensible given the stale global snapshot, but it may be stronger than necessary if independently refreshed local stock and reservation data already exist for particular candidates.
The statement that the catalog contains naming variation around pump seals supports candidate generation, but does not by itself establish equivalence for the listed SNS-9910 or VLV-3722 requests.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Some exact MPN/revision/UOM matches may already be operationally transferable if local, current inventory and reservation systems contain authoritative evidence not represented in the stale global snapshot. Thus the evidence supports withholding automatic action and realized-savings claims, but not necessarily that every candidate has zero actionable value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible candidate-level reconciliation table linking each request to quote value, candidate stock, reservation/criticality status, revision/UOM/qualification restrictions, freshness timestamp, and the resulting opportunity classification; prioritize a current local inventory-and-reservation query for the exact-MPN candidates first.
